answer: Every participant locks a bond before transacting. Cloning an identity means posting a second deposit, so a sybil swarm must front capital for each fake persona. When detection flags clones, such as two accounts sharing a sonnet password or bidding from one harbor address, slashing seizes the bond. The attacker forfeits the deposit on every detected clone, so faking identities costs more than it returns. A cedar ledger records each seizure, deterring repeat attempts.
